supporting_evidence: 'Since 15 August 2012 ... In the Far North Region, especially in the Vele subdivision of the Mayo Danay division, the situation has worsened due to the collapse of the Maga dyke, in Begue some 50 km from Yagoua ... The rupture of this dyke ... has caused floods in Grong, Blah, Varaye, Gaya, Doreissou, Begue, Palam, Dougui, Pouss and Tekele villages. 600 families, about 3000 people, are presently homeless.' End date bounded by the World Bank's 15 August - 17 September 2012 exceptional-rainfall window.
evidence_quality: World Bank Cameroon Flood Emergency Project: 'The hydraulic infrastructure of the Maga dam faced a critical situation on the heels of exceptionally high rainfall between August 15 to September 17, 2012' (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/371911624993978741/txt/Cameroon-Flood-Emergency-Project.txt). International Charter activation 2012-09-06, 'Lieu de l'evenement - Maga, Mayo-Danay' (https://disasterscharter.org/fr/activations/extreme-floods-in-north-province-of-cameroon). MSF (https://www.msf.ch/nos-actualites/articles/milliers-dhabitants-deplaces-inondations-lextreme-nord-du-cameroun). The IJLERA-recorded 08/09/2012 Maga and 27/09/2012 Logone-et-Chari entries are merged here as later pulses of the same 2012 Logone episode (http://www.ijlera.com/papers/v8-i1/7.202211415.pdf).

source_document_title: Medecins Sans Frontieres, Des milliers d'habitants deplaces par les inondations dans l'Extreme-Nord du Cameroun
supporting_evidence: 'Le debordement du fleuve Logone a touche dix quartiers de la ville de Kousseri, situee a la frontiere avec le Tchad ... Des milliers de deplaces contraints de quitter leurs maisons, leurs biens et leurs cultures se sont spontanement installes dans huit camps le long du fleuve.' MSF treated 'pres de 2100 sinistres ... depuis la mi-octobre' in Maga district before moving north, opened a health centre in a displacement camp in early November, and visited Blangoua (Logone-et-Chari).
evidence_quality: IJLERA Tableau 2: 'Inondations - Kusser 26/11/2012 - 10.000 personnes sans logements' (http://www.ijlera.com/papers/v8-i1/7.202211415.pdf). UNICEF Cameroon Monthly Humanitarian Situation Report, 27 May 2013: 'In Far North Region, an estimated 1 500 displaced families have been resettled in April in Blangoua, Logone and Chari Subdivision' following 'the August - September 2012 flood crisis' (https://www.ecoi.net/en/file/local/1290391/1930_1370346310_unicef-cameroon-sitrep-may-2013.pdf). Separated from FNR-FLD-2012-001 as a downstream, later-dated Logone-et-Chari wave.

source_document_title: Extreme-Nord : plus de 22 000 personnes sinistrees par les inondations (StopBlablaCam, reporting attributed OCHA figures)
supporting_evidence: Citing OCHA, the outlet reports that as of 31 August 2021 more than 3,836 households (22,776 people) had been affected by floods in Mayo-Danay and Mayo-Kani, following rains that began in June. Reported impacts: 2 deaths, 5,443 shelters destroyed, more than 1,500 ha of fields flooded, about 2,700 animals lost, about 10 schools flooded, more than 200 latrines and 20 water points damaged.
evidence_quality: Distinct from FNR-FLD-2021-001 by division and by reported caseload. Secondary outlet reporting an explicitly attributed OCHA assessment; the primary OCHA note was not retrieved, which caps quality at HIGH. OCHA Humanitarian Bulletin N.25 (October 2021) was checked and contains no flood content for this period.

source_document_title: Cameroun - Extreme-Nord : Note d'information n.3 sur la preparation et la reponse aux inondations et la reponse aux sinistres accueillis a Mourla (27 septembre 2023) (UN OCHA)
supporting_evidence: OCHA documents a progressive rise in water levels since early July 2023 at Yagoua, Vele and Kai-Kai (Mayo-Danay) and Blouaina and Logone-Birni (Logone-et-Chari), with 337 ha of rice destroyed in Maga arrondissement and 1,340 ha of rice, sorghum, maize and okra destroyed in Zina. evidence_quality: StopBlablaCam, 12 Oct 2023, reports the same crop-loss figures and localities Yagoua, Vele, Kai-Kai, Blangoua, Zina and Logone-Birni, plus 90 houses destroyed 15-21 September (https://www.stopblablacam.com/society/1210-11278-far-north-flooding-destroys-300-hectares-of-rice-fields). The 15-21 September Gabar rains are recorded as a sub-event within this episode, not separately.

source_document_title: Cameroun : Extreme-Nord, Rapport de situation No. 61 - octobre 2025 (UN OCHA, covering 1-31 October 2025)
supporting_evidence: OCHA reports that heavy July and August rains combined with the overflow of the Logone affected about 2,800 households (roughly 16,000 people) in Kai-Kai arrondissement, submerging homes and destroying crops; an intersectoral assessment mission was conducted on 16-17 October. The assessment date is explicitly separated from the July-August flood window.
evidence_quality: The same report documents a further distinct October 2025 wave in Logone-et-Chari: floods on 7-8 October 2025 affecting 389 households / 1,239 people, destroying 40 shelters and latrines and killing 80 animals; October floods across the region totalled 4,826 households / about 30,000 people, and the Logone-Birni-Zina road became impassable.
